title: Telemetry curation quarterly checklist and trace tags
summary: A pragmatic quarterly playbook for pruning, tagging and rotating telemetry (metrics + traces + dashboards) to control cost and reduce alert fatigue across inference services.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working checklist for the quarterly telemetry curation cycle. Goal: remove low-value signals, standardize trace tag conventions, and reassign ownership so dashboards are compact, cost-conscious, and actionable for token-serving systems.

Context / why now:
- Our query costs and dashboard noise have steadily increased with new model onboarding and routing logic.
- Multiple teams duplicate similar panels with slightly different filters, causing inconsistent incident responses.
- Traces are large and often lack stable tagging to attribute cold-cache vs runtime delays.

Scope (what this cycle touches):
- Dashboards: identify panels for deprecation, consolidation, or conversion to low-cardinality rollups.
- Metrics: flag custom histograms (many labels) for rework into aggregated quantiles or streaming summaries.
- Traces: enforce minimal span annotations and a small set of canonical trace tags for cross-team slicing.
- SLIs/SLOs: validate per-tenant and per-model SLIs remain fit-for-purpose and cost-aware.

Quarterly checklist (owner = rotation lead):
1) Inventory sweep (week 1)
   - Export dashboard list created/modified in last 12 months; mark panels with >5 unique breakouts or >5000 queries/month.
   - Gather owners for each dashboard; if none, tag as orphan.
   - Flag panels that query raw traces at high frequency for rewrite.

2) Cost-and-value triage (week 2)
   - For each panel, estimate monthly query/compute cost (use dashboard query-metering report).
   - Score value (1-5) based on: incident utility, product insight, legal/compliance need.
   - Panels with cost>threshold and value<=2 -> candidate for archive.

3) Consolidation pass (week 3)
   - Merge duplicates: prefer panel with standard variable set and stable filters.
   - Replace expensive ad-hoc histograms with pre-aggregated quantiles or sampled rollups.
   - Convert high-cardinality tenant breakdowns into sampled top-N with “other” bucket.

4) Trace tagging and span hygiene (week 3-4)
   - Enforce canonical trace tags: service, request_id, tenant_id (when permitted), model_variant, route, cache_hit (true|false), batching_group (optional).
   - Small guideline: limit trace-level freeform labels to 3 keys. All other attributes should be numeric metrics or event logs.
   - Identify spans >200KB or >50 spans per request: instrument early returns or reduce internal span detail.

5) SLI/SLO sanity check (week 4)
   - Verify SLI definitions cover production traffic patterns: 99th latency slice, tail-per-tenant SLI, correctness/regression indicators.
   - If SLO burn is noisy due to cold starts, add a warmup-excluded bucket or warmup-aware alerting policy.

6) Ownership and runbook updates (end of cycle)
   - Assign explicit owner (team + person) or move to archive.
   - Update dashboard readme with expected usage, query cost estimate, and emergency contact.
   - Rollout small communication to oncall and product stakeholders summarizing removed/changed panels.

Trace tag conventions (proposal):
- service: short service name (e.g. infer-router, kv-cache, model-exec)
- request_id: GUID for the API request (always present)
- tenant_id: obfuscated tenant id or tenant-hash; only present for allowed teams (PII rules)
- model_variant: stable model id/version (e.g. gptx-13b-v1)
- route: API route (text.generate, embeddings.create)
- cache_hit: true|false|null (null when not applicable)
- batch_size: numeric (0 or greater)
- region: cloud region code when relevant (us-west1, eu-central1)

Note: privacy control -> tenant_id must be redacted for public dashboards and only included in internal traces stored behind KMS.

Metric definition examples (non-nested canonical strings):
- inference.latency_ms.p50: real-time P50 end-to-end (ingest->response) in ms, computed on raw request latencies, aggregated as type=histogram->quantile.
- inference.kv_cache.hit_rate: ratio (hits/requests) for KV cache lookups computed per-model per-hour.
- model.exec.tokens_per_second: measured at model-exec span boundary; measured over sliding 1m windows.

Dashboard pruning heuristics (practical rules):
- If a panel hasn't been used in the last 90 days by any oncall or product owner, archive unless it supports compliance.
- If panel requires a join across >3 high-cardinality labels, either pre-aggregate or remove.
- Panels that are "slice-of-the-week" should be turned into scheduled reports instead of live panels.

Sampling and retention recommendations:
- Traces: keep full traces for 14 days for production heavy paths, 7 days for low-traffic services, and 30 days for compliance-critical flows (when necessary).
- Metrics: keep raw high-resolution metrics for 30 days, then rollup to 1m/5m buckets for 365 days.
- For unusually high-cardinality attributes, use bloom filters or attribute hashing + cardinality counters instead of raw string retention.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive can we be with tenant_id removal before SLO debug burden grows? (stakeholders: security, SRE, solutions-eng)
- Do we add a low-cost cold-cache SLI that explicitly excludes the first N requests after model spin-up?
- Who funds the rewrite work for high-cost dashboards owned by cross-functional teams?

Action items (next steps):
- Arjun: run the dashboard export and produce query-cost CSV by 2026-02-21.
- Maya: draft tenant-tagging privacy policy and present to SecOps by 2026-02-28.
- Lena: prototype query rollup for histogram panels and PR to obs-infra by 2026-03-07.
- Connor: update oncall runbook template to call out archived-dashboard escalation path by 2026-03-03.

Quick wins (low effort):
- Add owner tag to top 200 dashboards with a single bulk-edit.
- Convert three heavy histograms to pre-aggregated quantiles for router service.
- Add a small "dashboard-cost" widget to the observability home to surface the top 10 cost drivers.

Fallback / rollback plan:
- Archive into a tagged folder with a 30-day freeze window; allow restore without approval for first 14 days.
- Maintain a short changelog entry for each pruned panel with reason and contact.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and conservative for the first cycle. We should aim to remove ~10-15% of panels with the highest cost:benefit gap.
- Please comment inline with specific dashboards or metric names you think should be exempt.

References and links:
- Telemetry inventory (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Telemetry+Inventory
- Cost-metering dashboard: dashboards/observability/query-costs
